whyTitle: Why do forms ask for a 100KB photo?
whyP1: A 100KB cap keeps application servers fast and storage costs down when thousands of applicants upload photos at once — which is why it's such a common limit on Indian government recruitment portals. SSC CGL, UPSC, IBPS bank exams, and several state PSC and railway recruitment forms all specify a photo size limit in this range, and uploads over the limit are simply rejected at submission.
whyP2: The problem is that a photo straight off a phone camera is usually 2-5MB — 20-50x too large. Resizing dimensions alone doesn't reliably hit an exact KB target, which is what this tool does directly: pick 100KB, upload your photo, and download a file sized right for the form.
howP: Your photo is re-encoded to land at or under 100KB while keeping text and faces readable in a form-style image, usually with no visible quality loss. If you need a different size, the same tool supports custom targets like 20KB or 50KB too.
diveTitle: What to know about the 100KB headroom
diveSubtitle: Why this cap is used when clarity matters more than minimal size.
dive1Title: Why 100KB is used when detail needs to stay legible
dive1Desc: 100KB gives significantly more room than 20KB or 50KB, which matters for scanned documents with fine text or certificates where small print needs to stay readable after compression — not just a face photo where a lower cap is usually enough.
dive2Title: How exact-target compression preserves more at a higher cap
dive2Desc: The same highest-quality-that-fits approach applies here, but with a 100KB budget the tool can retain noticeably more visual detail than it could at 20KB or 50KB before it needs to compress further.
dive3Title: Best suited for scans and documents, not just photos
dive3Desc: Certificate scans, ID document images, and marksheets often need enough resolution for small text to stay sharp — a 20KB or 50KB target can blur fine print, while 100KB usually keeps it legible.
dive4Title: Quality vs. dimension trade-off at this size
dive4Desc: At 100KB, most standard photos and document scans reach the target through quality adjustment alone, without needing to shrink pixel dimensions — dimension reduction typically only kicks in for unusually large or high-resolution source files.
dive5Title: Where a 100KB limit typically shows up
dive5Desc: Passport and visa application photo uploads, government ID document scans, and certificate/marksheet uploads for verification commonly specify 100KB or a similar range — check your specific form, since document scans often get a higher allowance than plain photos.
dive6Title: When even 100KB isn't the right fit
dive6Desc: If a form has no strict KB cap and you just want a smaller file without hitting an exact number, our general compress-image tool with a percentage-based reduction may give you a better quality-to-size balance than forcing an exact byte target.
faq1Q: Which exams and forms need a 100KB photo?
faq1A: Many Indian government exam and recruitment portals — SSC, UPSC, IBPS, Railway RRB, and various state PSC forms — cap the photo upload at 100KB. The exact limit varies by form, so double-check the instructions on your specific application before uploading.
faq2Q: Will compressing to 100KB make my photo blurry?
faq2A: Not noticeably for a standard ID or application photo. The tool lowers JPEG quality first and reduces pixel dimensions slightly only if it has to, so text and facial features stay readable.
faq3Q: What image formats can I compress to 100KB?
faq3A: JPG, PNG, and WEBP are all supported. Most exam portals ask for JPG specifically — if yours does, just upload your photo in any format and the compressed download will be sized correctly regardless.
faq4Q: Do I need to sign up or install anything?
faq4A: No. Upload your photo, get your 100KB file, done — no software to install, and the file is deleted from our servers automatically afterward.
faq5Q: Can I compress multiple photos at once?
faq5A: Yes — up to 2 images at a time on the free plan (10 on Starter, 20 on Pro). Each one is compressed to 100KB individually, and you can download them all when they're ready.
